description.invocation: Measured invocation: qwen_inference.infer(model, inputs, new_tokens=32) (qwen_inference.py:15-41) under torch.inference_mode for the 'interactive' workload row (workloads.json qwen_inference.workloads[0]: id=interactive, batch=1, prompt_tokens=256, new_tokens=32). Inputs are the chat-templated fixed prompt tokens repeated/truncated to 256, resident on GPU as a batch=1 tensor. One unit = one full fixed-length greedy generation: prefill forward with use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1, argmax of the last position, explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() at the first-token-ready boundary, then 31 cached decode steps (EOS stopping disabled by the explicit loop). Model/tokenizer loading, input preparation, reference capture runs, correctness checks, reference tensor saving, warmup, repeats and --profile tracing are setup or measurement infrastructure outside this unit.

workload.prompt: Explain how a computer executes a neural network and why memory access, arithmetic and communication affect performance. Use concrete examples.

notes: Command provenance: intent.json supplies 'python qwen_inference.py --assets /root/autodl-tmp/c3-qwen3-4b-operator-goals/assets/Qwen3-4B/1cfa9a7208912126459214e8b04321603b3df60c --output /tmp/original-qwen', run from the repository root with /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python (README.md; worker-environment.json).

ttft_ms is produced by the source itself (qwen_inference.py:37) as the interval from the pre-forward synchronize to the explicit first-token-ready synchronize after prefill+argmax (qwen_inference.py:16-24); this is the completion boundary of the objective. decode_ms, end_to_end_ms, decode_tokens_per_second, generated_tokens_per_second and peak_allocated_bytes are also reported per sample but only ttft_ms is the objective here; the interactive row's decode goal is a separate goal, not a constraint of this request.

The full generation workload is preserved: the timed unit always completes all 32 tokens (prefill + 31 cached decode steps); only prefill/first-token latency is optimized, the decode loop is not truncated.

Discrete exact comparison: generated greedy tokens must satisfy torch.equal (qwen_inference.py:62) - exact match required, no tolerance. Captured per-step last-token logits (stacked shape [batch, new_tokens, vocab]) are compared with torch.testing.assert_close at atol=rtol=0.02 (common.py:74-76, qwen_inference.py:61); the +1 corruption negative control must be rejected (common.py:79-84).

Precision/state policy: BF16 weights with attn_implementation='sdpa' (qwen_inference.py:49); TF32 disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark False, seed 20261020, 4 torch threads (common.py:34-42); use_cache=True with the KV cache carried across decode steps, logits_to_keep=1.

Workload and quality field names (id, batch, prompt_tokens, new_tokens, goals, prompt; logits_atol, logits_rtol, require_exact_greedy_tokens) are copied unchanged from workloads.json qwen_inference; the 'offline' (batch=8) row and held_out_workloads (long_prompt) are not part of this task.

Reference construction (two capture runs, one with teacher forcing), correctness checks, {id}-reference.pt saving, warmup/repeats statistics, summarize() and profile_once() belong to the benchmark harness, not the work repeated per measurement; --profile adds a separately traced diagnostic run and is not requested by the command.

Single-process single-GPU task: model is placed with .cuda() and configure() pins device 0; no process group, no NCCL, hence device_count=1, no distributed_backend and no required communication observations. Worker binds the leased GPU UUID from deployment.json.

assumptions: The default --workloads (repository workloads.json) is used since the intent command does not override it.
Warmup=2 and repeats=5 come from common.py argument defaults, matching the README suite invocation.

The source imposes no baseline_ratio/threshold constraint on ttft_ms for the interactive row, so objective.constraints is empty; decode throughput preservation is not additionally constrained beyond keeping the full generation workload and the correctness checks.
The output directory /tmp/original-qwen from the command is harness output, not an asset; results and reference tensors are written there by the harness.
EOS early stopping is already disabled by the fixed explicit loop, so generation length is exactly new_tokens=32 regardless of decoded content.
